comments.body:
## OPERATOR DECISION: option (b) — loud, intentional skip

The operator has chosen **(b)**: the `browser_runner` tier is NOT to be run in CI. It is to be
recorded as a deliberate local-only skip, with a check that fails if the tier is silently skipped
WITHOUT the recorded opt-out.

This resolves the fork the ticket names and unblocks implementation.

## What this decision does and does not concede

It does NOT concede that the current state is acceptable. The defect this ticket describes is that
**absence of execution is indistinguishable from coverage** — CI reports green while a whole class
of assertions never ran. Choosing (b) fixes that by making the non-execution EXPLICIT and
enforced; it does not fix it by leaving things as they are. A silent self-skip and a recorded
deliberate skip are different states, and only the second is acceptable.

Concretely, ACs 1, 3, 4 and 5 remain in force and AC2 (the (a) branch) drops away:

- AC1 — the disposition is recorded in the tree.
- AC3 — a check FAILS if the tier is silently skipped without the recorded opt-out. Demonstrate by
  removing the marker and observing RED. This is the anti-vacuity criterion and is the heart of
  the fix; a marker that nothing enforces would just relocate the original defect.
- AC4 — the summary a reader sees distinguishes "deliberately not run" from "passed".
- AC5 — portable: the chosen behaviour works in a checkout with no CI provider. This is the
  blocking `project.portability` plan-review criterion, so a solution keyed to GitHub Actions
  specifically will not pass review.

## Supporting rationale

Change 2600 deliberately moved `playwright` to `optionalDependencies` and provisions with
`--omit=optional` for selections containing no browser test, cutting the cold install from 15
packages / 30M to 11 / 12M. Option (a) would have re-added that cost plus a large cached browser
binary on the critical path. Given rebar's surface is a library, a CLI and an MCP server, browser
behaviour is not load-bearing enough to justify that on every run.

The tier remains available and meaningful LOCALLY, which is where it was already effectively
running. Nothing about this decision removes coverage that was actually being obtained — it makes
honest the fact that CI was never obtaining it.

## Narration moved out of the description (P4 admission limit)

The description crossed the 8000-char plan-review admission cap, so the settled rationale
lives here instead of in the plan.

**Why option (a) was rejected on cost.** Change `2600` deliberately moved `playwright` to
`optionalDependencies` and provisions with `--omit=optional` for selections containing no
browser test, cutting the cold install from 15 packages / 30M to 11 / 12M. Option (a) would
have re-added that plus a large cached Chromium binary to the critical path of every run.
rebar's shipped surface is a library, a CLI and an MCP server; the editor bundle's runtime
behaviour is not load-bearing enough to buy that on every build.

**What the decision does not concede.** The defect is that absence of execution is
indistinguishable from coverage. Choosing (b) fixes that by making the non-execution explicit
AND enforced, not by leaving things as they are. The record is not decorative: without it the
tier fails. That is the difference between this and "add a comment saying we meant to".

**Two review iterations shaped the design.** The first plan-review BLOCKED on G1G2/G6: it found
that two browser-tier skip sites outside `conftest.py` — `library_editor_server`
(`tests/e2e/test_editor_library.py`) and `batch_library_editor_server`
(`tests/e2e/test_editor_batch_library.py`) — were unenumerated, and that an AST scan scoped to
`conftest.py` could not see them. Both are now routed through the guard and the scan covers
every module under `tests/e2e/`. That finding is worth recording because it is the same shape
as the original defect: a check whose partition misses a value it was never told about.

For the same reason the scan was widened a second time, pre-emptively, to `pytest.mark.skipif`
— the other way a browser test could vanish without ever reaching the fixture guard. There are
zero uses today, so it costs nothing and closes the class rather than the instance.

## Implemented and pushed — Gerrit change 2652

Commit `2d889f40c237` on `bug-337e-browser-tier-optout`, base `e510c64dbcb6`.
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2652

### Evidence

**AC3 — RED without the marker (the anti-vacuity criterion).** Demonstrated twice, at both
levels, with Chromium made unreachable (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` pointed at an empty dir):

- With `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml` present:
  `pytest tests/e2e/test_editor_browser.py -q` -> `6 skipped, 1 warning`, each reason
  `BROWSER TIER DELIBERATELY NOT RUN (local-only) - Chromium will not launch ... These
  browser assertions did NOT execute; this is a recorded decision, not a pass. Why:
  browser-tier-optout.toml (ticket 337e-b558-17a2-49bd).`
- With the record MOVED AWAY, same command: `6 errors`, each
  `Failed: BROWSER TIER SILENTLY SKIPPED - Chromium will not launch ... This tier did not
  execute and nothing in the tree licenses that.` The unit suite goes from `12 passed` to
  `3 failed`. Record restored afterwards.

**AC4 — the summary distinguishes.** Under plain `-q` (no `-rs`), the warnings summary
carries the banner and the full recorded reasoning; a reader of a "green" run is told the
tier did not run.

**Local verification** (targeted; `make verify` deliberately not run per the load
constraint): `make lint` rc=0, `make typecheck` rc=0 (762 files),
`check_mechanism_delta.py --check` `new=0 increased=0`, `check_complexity_baseline.py
--check` `new=0 increased=0`, `pytest tests/e2e tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py`
`45 passed`, `pytest tests/unit -m repo_policy` `22 passed`, plus the six modules that
reference `tests/e2e` `86 passed`. No baseline file edited; the only `.github/` path in the
diff is `_build-and-test.yml` (comment only).

**Plan-review:** certified at `e510c64dbcb681fd8e14050a854dfce86f488faf`, after two BLOCK
iterations (G1G2/G6 on the two unenumerated in-module fixtures, then P4 on description
length). Both remediated, not forced.

Not closed and not submitted: awaiting `LLM-Review` and `Verified`.

comments.body:
## Patchset 2 — `Verified -1` root-caused; TWO distinct causes, not one

Change 2652, patchset 2 = `4bba9fbb9ebf` (same Change-Id).

### Cause 1 (mine, real, fixed): the announcement warning killed the xdist controller

The three pytest cells did NOT fail at collection. They ran, then died mid-run. Verbatim from
`pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)`:

```
INTERNALERROR>   File ".../xdist/workermanage.py", line 474, in unserialize_warning_message
INTERNALERROR>     mod = importlib.import_module(data["message_module"])
INTERNALERROR> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_browser_tier'
[gw0] node down: <ExceptionInfo ModuleNotFoundError("No module named '_browser_tier'")>
...
INTERNALERROR> KeyError: <WorkerController gw0>
1 failed, 34 passed, 1 skipped in 78.56s
```

An xdist worker serializes a warning by its **class's module name**, and the CONTROLLER
re-imports that module to rebuild it. `BrowserTierNotRunWarning` was defined in
`tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py`: importable on the worker (pytest puts `tests/e2e` on the
worker's path when it loads that conftest) and **not** on the controller, whose path never
includes it. So the first licensed skip took the node down and cascaded into an
`INTERNALERROR`. The mechanism built to make the tier's absence loud was loud enough to abort
the run announcing it — exactly the distinction between "loud in the RESULT" and "loud enough
to kill the session".

It never showed locally because every verification run was single-process; the CI lane uses
`-n 4 --dist worksteal`.

**Reproduced locally, then fixed and re-verified:**

```
pytest tests -n 2 --dist worksteal -k "editor_renders_diagram_panel... or test_committed_record_is_complete"
  BEFORE: INTERNALERROR ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_browser_tier'   (session dead)
  AFTER:  1 passed, 7 skipped, 1 warning in 18.36s
pytest tests/e2e tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py -n 2 --dist worksteal  ->  46 passed
```

**Fix:** the category is now `pytest.PytestWarning` — an installed class both ends can import,
the same channel `tests/conftest.py` already uses for its xdist-safe timing spans. The banner
and the full recorded reasoning are unchanged, so AC4 still holds.

**New regression test** `test_the_warning_category_is_importable_by_the_xdist_controller`
probes the invariant the way the controller does: an isolated interpreter (`python -I`, which
ignores cwd and `PYTHONPATH`) must be able to import the module the category is defined in.
Demonstrated RED against the old design — restoring a tests-local category makes it fail with
`the browser-tier warning category lives in '_browser_tier_under_test', which an xdist
controller cannot import`.

### Cause 2 (not mine, environmental): the bwrap sandbox cell

`sandbox enforcement (Linux bwrap, gating)` failed with `Process completed with exit code 100`
in the step `docker run --rm --privileged ubuntu:24.04 bash -c 'set -e; apt-get update -qq
>/dev/null 2>&1; apt-get install -y -qq bubblewrap >/dev/null 2>&1; ...'`. 100 is apt-get's
error code, and the step suppresses all apt output, so the log shows only the exit. The step
runs a stock `ubuntu:24.04` container and installs from the Ubuntu archive; it reads nothing
from the patchset, and this change touches only `tests/`, `docs/` and one YAML comment. The
same job was `success` on run `33938327905` eight minutes earlier. So: a transient package-
manager fault, not a second defect and not a consequence of cause 1. No `recheck` was posted —
patchset 2 re-runs CI anyway.

Worth noting as a separate observation: that step's `>/dev/null 2>&1` means an apt failure
here can never say why. Same shape as this ticket — a gate whose failure is unreadable.

Not closed, not submitted.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

No workflow step runs `npx playwright install chromium`, so the `browser_runner` fixture
self-skips on "Chromium unavailable" in CI: the browser tier never executes there. A skipped
tier looks exactly like a passing one in the summary, so CI reports green while a whole class
of assertions never ran and nothing tells the reader. Surfaced while implementing bug
`9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`; pre-existing.

## Decision (recorded by the operator in a comment on this ticket)

**Option (b): the tier is NOT run in CI, and its non-execution becomes explicit and enforced.**
It stays local-only, which is where it was already effectively running. Option (a) —
provisioning Chromium in CI — is rejected on cost (see the operator comment). AC2 of the
original draft, the (a) branch, is dropped; ACs 1, 3, 4 and 5 remain and are restated below.
A silent self-skip and a recorded deliberate skip are different states, and only the second is
acceptable: this is not closed by adding a comment to the fixture.

## Approach

A **recorded opt-out** becomes the tier's licence not to run, and every non-execution path
consults it.

1. **The record** — `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml`: a TOML declaration with
   `scope = "local-only"`, the deciding ticket id, and a non-blank `reason`. It lives in the
   tree, is greppable, and is what a future reader finds.
2. **The enforcement** — `tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py` exposes `tier_unavailable(detail)`.
   With a complete record it raises a **loud skip** whose reason begins
   `BROWSER TIER DELIBERATELY NOT RUN` and names the record, the deciding ticket and the
   concrete cause. With the record **absent, unparseable, or blank-reasoned** it raises
   `pytest.fail`. Removing the marker therefore turns every browser test RED.
3. **The wiring** — every fixture a browser test depends on replaces its bare
   `pytest.skip(...)` with `tier_unavailable(...)`: `browser_runner`, `editor_server` and
   `editor_server_batch` in `tests/e2e/conftest.py`, **plus** the two in-module server
   fixtures `library_editor_server` and `batch_library_editor_server`, which gate on the same
   `assets_available()` condition and are consumed by browser tests. Leaving those two
   unguarded would keep exactly the silent path this ticket exists to remove.
4. **The summary** — `tier_unavailable` warns through pytest's warnings channel (shown even
   under `-q`, grouped for identical messages), so a reader of a green run is told the tier
   did not run and that this was decided, not missed. The category is
   `pytest.PytestWarning` — an **installed** class, never one defined under `tests/`, because
   an xdist worker serializes a warning by its class's module name and the controller
   re-imports it; a tests-local category is unimportable there and takes the whole session
   down. The per-test skip reason stays short; the warning carries the reasoning in full.
5. **Documentation** — `docs/workflow-editor.md` says all E2E tiers are "opt-in and
   self-skipping", which stops being true; it records the local-only disposition instead. A
   comment in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` beside the e2e provisioning step says
   why no browser-provisioning step exists and points at the record. No workflow step is
   added or removed.

**Portability.** The mechanism reads one repository file: no environment variable, no CI
detection, no provider API. Assume no CI provider is present; nothing branches on one, so a
checkout without CI behaves identically — loud skip with the record, hard failure without it.

**Why not an env-var or a gate script.** An env-var opt-out is per-run configuration, so it is
exactly the state that can be forgotten and revert to an accidental skip; the record must be a
durable tree artefact. A `scripts/check_*.py` gate could only assert the record exists — it
cannot observe that the tier failed to execute, which is what AC3 names. The enforcement has
to sit at the skip site, in the fixture.

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml` (new) — the recorded opt-out.
- `tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py` (new) — record loader, `tier_unavailable`, the warning channel.
- `tests/e2e/conftest.py` — route the three conftest fixtures through `tier_unavailable`.
- `tests/e2e/test_editor_library.py`, `tests/e2e/test_editor_batch_library.py` — route their
  in-module server fixtures' bare skips through `tier_unavailable`.
- `tests/e2e/test_editor_browser.py` — docstring only ("self-skips" stops being true).
- `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` — its `_replica` helper must copy the guard and
  the record into the sandbox e2e tree (a replica without the record exercises a different
  contract), and its browser skip-reason assertion moves to the new banner.
- `tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py` (new) — the enforcement's own tests.
- `docs/workflow-editor.md` — record the disposition where the tiers are described.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — comment only.

No `src/rebar` changes: test-infrastructure and documentation work.

## Testing

New tests in `tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py`, needing neither Node nor a browser, so
they run on every CI cell:

- **Happy path** — the committed record parses and is complete.
- **Loud skip** — with the record present, `tier_unavailable("Chromium will not launch")`
  raises `Skipped` naming the banner, the ticket, the record file and the cause.
- **Failure path (anti-vacuity)** — with the record path pointed at a non-existent file,
  `tier_unavailable(...)` raises `Failed`, **not** `Skipped`: the automated form of "remove
  the marker and observe RED".
- **Edge, incomplete record** — parametrized over empty, wrong-table, blank-reason,
  missing-reason and unparseable records: none licences a skip; each fails like an absent one.
- **Portability scan** — an AST scan asserts `_browser_tier.py` imports no `os` and names no
  CI provider.
- **Announcement safety** — an isolated interpreter (`python -I`, the xdist controller's own
  path view) must be able to import the module the warning category is defined in, so the
  tier's loud absence can never abort the run it is announcing into.
- **Regression scans** — an AST scan over every module under `tests/e2e/` asserts no function
  calls `pytest.skip(...)` directly, except `bpmn_harness` (the round-trip tier, a different
  disposition) and the guard itself; a second asserts no module uses `pytest.mark.skipif`, the
  other shape in which a browser test could vanish without reaching the guard.

`tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` drives the real conftest through a nested pytest
run and stays green, with its failed-provisioning case now asserting the loud banner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 1. `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml` exists, names the deciding ticket, and states why
      the tier is local-only. Checked by `test_committed_record_is_complete`.
- [ ] 3. With the record absent, a browser-tier non-execution FAILS rather than skips. Checked
      by `test_absent_record_fails_instead_of_skipping` and by the manual delete-the-record
      demonstration recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] 4. The run's output distinguishes "deliberately not run" from "passed": the skip reason
      begins `BROWSER TIER DELIBERATELY NOT RUN` and a warning carrying that banner appears in
      the warnings summary, without destabilising the run. Checked by
      `test_skip_reason_is_loud_and_names_the_record`,
      `test_a_licensed_non_execution_warns_so_the_summary_shows_it` and
      `test_the_warning_category_is_importable_by_the_xdist_controller`.
- [ ] 5. The guard reads only a repository file, so a checkout with no CI provider behaves
      identically. Checked by `test_guard_reads_no_environment_and_knows_no_ci_provider`.
- [ ] 6. No e2e module retains an unguarded non-execution path. Checked by
      `test_no_browser_fixture_falls_back_to_a_bare_skip` and
      `test_no_e2e_module_hides_a_test_behind_a_bare_skipif`.
- [ ] 7. `pytest tests/e2e tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py -n 2` exits 0 (under xdist,
      which is how CI runs it).
- [ ] 8. `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] 9. `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] 10. `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists no path under `.github/` other than
      `_build-and-test.yml`, so no ratchet baseline was edited.
